name: Artist-family home meals, Raghurajpur
signature_dish: Home-cooked Odia thali — dalma, pakhala, machha besara
why_it_matters: Raghurajpur is a heritage crafts village of about 120 pattachitra-artist families and has no proper standalone restaurant — food facilities in the village are described by tourism sources as very basic. The honest way to eat here is a home-cooked Odia meal arranged with an artist family, several of whom run informal homestays. It is the village's only genuine dining experience, and it doubles as a way to spend time with the painters.
insider_tip: There is no walk-in restaurant — a meal must be arranged in advance through an artist family or a homestay, ideally the day before. Pair it with watching pattachitra or palm-leaf work being done. For a quick bite without arrangement, eat in Chandanpur on the access road or back in Puri.
signature_address: Raghurajpur Heritage Crafts Village, near Chandanpur, Puri district, Odisha 752012

name: Hotel Padmalaya, Chandanpur (Raghurajpur access road)
signature_dish: Chuda kadamba with dalma — Chandanpur's signature breakfast
why_it_matters: Chandanpur is the junction village on the Puri-Konark road where the turn-off to Raghurajpur lies, and it is the practical meal stop for visitors to the craft village, which has no restaurant of its own. Hotel Padmalaya in Chandanpur is documented for chuda kadamba — a sweet beaten-rice dish mixed with rabri and chhena — served with spicy dalma, the village's signature breakfast.
insider_tip: This is a Chandanpur address, explicitly labelled — not inside Raghurajpur itself, but the nearest practical place to eat when visiting the craft village. Come for breakfast: chuda kadamba with dalma is the local speciality and is best in the morning. Pair a Raghurajpur visit with a Chandanpur breakfast stop.
signature_address: Chandanpur, Puri-Konark Road, Puri district, Odisha 752012
